references.text: The Ammonites crossed the Jordan to fight against Judah, Benjamin, and the house of Ephraim, showing the same conflict between Ammon and Israel.
The Ammonites gathered and camped in Gilead, while the Israelites gathered at Mizpah, which is the direct context before Jephthah was called.
Earlier, Eglon, king of Moab, gathered the Ammonites and Amalekites against Israel, showing a pattern of Ammonite aggression.
Nahash, king of the Ammonites, besieged Jabesh in Gilead, showing continued hostility between Ammon and Israel during Saul's time.
The king of the Ammonites died, and his son Hanun became king, leading to new conflict with Israel under David.
God instructed Israel not to attack the Ammonites because He had given them their land as an inheritance, providing background for the complicated relationship.
